lines: My memories reach back to an age long past.
The gods who govern life,
and the gods who govern the order of things—my fathers—at war:
the sorrowful fate of those who could not trust each other's ways.
My father bore me, in whom no life dwells.
That god bore you, who nurtures life.
And the hand that reached out was offered to me.
Ah… I know your heart.
I know your anger, and your sorrow.
I know the great love you gave to small lives.
But you do not know the tears I shed.
Your wrath and that god's gave birth to a great sin.
You become one with me, and your body shatters.
My heart and my body both grew unstable.
But I do not mind.
For I was able to welcome
the beloved ones you held so dear.
My fathers banished that god,
and I was reborn to be cleansed of my taint—
though I never thought of it as a taint—
to live on with these children, all you left behind.
And yet,
now you…
My memories reach back to an age long past.
The gods who govern life—my fathers—
at war with the gods who govern the order of things:
a shameful deed of those steeped in power and greed.
That god bore you, in whom no life dwells.
My father bore me, who nurtures life.
Yet the hand that reached out was offered to you.
Ah… I cannot understand the hearts of the gods.
None of them will even look upon small lives.
They do not know the wailing of those who can only pray.
But I alone knew those children's tears.
I gave birth to a great sin.
Vowing that we would meet again one day, I shatter.
My mind grows clouded, sinking into darkness.
But I do not mind.
If those children can live on—
for I was able to save the ones I love.
My father was banished,
and you were reborn, as if to hide the gods' cruelty,
cradling the children I had raised.
And now,
I…
